To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
microglia in brain slices cultured under serum‐free condition have a ramified morphology and a reduced capacity to produce superoxide anions and to phagocytose latex beads.

1) Microglia in the tissue slice culture have the same morphological and functional properties as microglia in monolayer cultures, 2) microglia in tissue slice cultures are functionally down‐regulating after 10 days, and 3) the organotypic tissue slice culture system is a useful model system for examining microglial interactions with neurons and other brain cells.

1. microglia in slice cultures have functional characteristics that are similar to microglia in vivo; and 2. the microglial functions are downregulated with prolonged culture of the slice, which may be a result of interactions of microglial cells with the surrounding tissue in the slice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the function and development of microglia and astrocytes in the normal and diseased central nervous system.
the study of the microglial response to injury in the central nervous system (CNS) and its potential role in the development of secondary injury.
the role of the immune response in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microglial cell in the adult brain is a dynamic cell that is capable of a number of functions, but that the microglia are not a homogenous population of cells.
microglia are the major phagocyte of the central nervous system.
the microglia in culture is not the same as microglia in vivo, and that microglial function in vivo is dependent on its microenvironment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that organotypic slice culturing of the brain can be used to study the interactions between neurons, astrocytes and microglia in a way that is similar to the in vivo brain.
we have developed a system for studying microglia in their normal environment, and that the microglia in this system behave as we expected.
microglia in tissue slice culture at 4 DIV are functionally active and resemble microglia isolated from the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microglia can be cultured in a way that allows them to retain their in vivo functions.
the microglia in our slice culture system are very active and phagocytic at 4 DIV, but by 10 DIV the microglia are very quiescent and phagocytosis is reduced.
we have developed a model system to study the interactions of microgila with neurons and other cells in the brain.
